summary.intent: Repair the broken pre-push hook chain, land an AGENTS.md docs PR, then continue the PR-body redesign: clean up merged worktrees and branches, wire markers and the not-releasing list into the PR body, and start the CLI I/O consolidation and grouped changelog work.
summary.outcome: The pre-push hook chain was repaired and tested both ways, and docs PR #472 merged along with #470. Stale worktrees and merged branches were cleaned up. The `feat/pr-body-attention` wiring was built with passing tests and mutation checks, and a full verify run was started. The CLI io and changelog agents were launched, and the final verify result is not shown in the transcript.

repo: Entire's `pre-push.pre-entire` wrapper chains to `pre-push.pre-entire.pre-entire-brain`. That file was missing, so `just pre-push` never ran on push. Copying the original hook to that name fixed it without disabling Entire's checkpoint push.
Re-running `just hooks` would overwrite Entire's pre-push wrapper and switch off its checkpoint push, which the user wants kept.

AGENTS.md verification rules: run `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, run `just ci` before marking ready, judge success by exit code and never by grepping, and sign all commits without `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `verification.reason` must be `valid`.
The uncovered-changes detector's `covered` input must be the plan's bumped packages, not only changeset names. Otherwise cascade-bumped packages show up as false positives.
The graph crate has 1074 lib tests, and `emit_preview_tests` in callisto-cli checks that the release preview equals the plan.
Wiring the attention feature touches `release_preview.rs` and `pr_body.rs`, so these changes should land one PR at a time rather than stacked.

Branches `chore/routine-crates-update`, `docs/next-work-plan`, `docs/spec-rewrite`, `feat/read-tag-hints`, `fix/native-resolution`, `fix/operation-id-display`, `fix/publish-output-visible`, `perf/parallel-history` and `stack/docs-v1` carry commits that exist nowhere else on origin. Their tips were recorded to `.claude/plans/archive/remote-branch-tips-2026-11-08.txt`.

code.finding: In the struct initializer, `changes` was moved before the `findings` expression borrowed it. The fix was to compute `findings` first.
Using `?` inside a `.map` closure cannot return from the handler when building the release preview. It was restructured into an explicit `match`.

workflow: After changing a gate, run a negative test: break formatting on purpose and confirm the chain exits non-zero, then restore the file.
Back up files before changing hooks and give a one-file undo path.
Ignored files such as `.claude/plans` live inside a worktree, so removing the worktree deletes them. Check what survives and re-create anything lost.
For multi-file edits, use an all-or-nothing script that checks every replacement before writing any file.
Mutation checks restored from a backup copy show that new tests catch regressions.
Delegated agents were given no git access, so their work is reviewed and committed by the main session by reading their worktree files directly.
The environment refused a bulk delete of remote branches holding unique commits. Recording the branch tips first keeps the choice safe either way.

friction: The first remote branch delete failed and had to be retried. The retry succeeded.
The bulk delete of stale remote branches was refused because they hold unmerged unique commits.
The plan file and archive patches were written under a worktree that was then removed, so they had to be recreated in the main checkout.
Git could not be run inside the markers agent's worktree, so its files were read directly.
Two compile and test errors (a borrow/move ordering problem and `?` in a closure) took extra iterations.
Entire's change states for merged PRs still say `open`, which needs a fix on Entire's side.
open_items: Delete or resolve the nine stale remote branches that hold unique commits. Only their tips have been recorded.
Check the result of the final `verify.sh` run for `feat/pr-body-attention`, then commit, sign, push and open the PR.
Review and commit the CLI io consolidation and the grouped changelog layout from the two launched agents.
The grouped changelog changes the committed changelog format, so the user needs to decide on it.
Labels (`release: ready|breaking|…`, `bump:`, `registry:`) are deferred until the findings exist.
The global `CLAUDE.md` verify rule was not applied and awaits user approval.
